body:
## Category

- [x] CI/CD Workflow (GitHub Actions)
- [x] Repository Configuration (branch rules, templates)

## Description

The scheduled Dependabot **nuget** updater hits the 1-hour GitHub job timeout before producing PRs. Without successful runs, security advisories against existing dependencies don't reach `main` automatically — they have to be patched by hand whenever a new GHSA lands.

This was discovered while investigating the workflow failures of 2026-04-24 to 2026-04-27 (CI Full, CodeQL, Benchmarks, Load Tests, Mutation Tests). All 5 failed because three packages with new GHSA advisories tripped `NU1902`/`NU1904` and `TreatWarningsAsErrors` escalates them to errors. Dependabot should have raised the bump PR before the audit fired in CI; instead the most recent nuget run was cancelled at the 1h mark (see Current Behavior).

## Component Affected

- **File(s)**: [`.github/dependabot.yml`](.github/dependabot.yml), [`Directory.Packages.props`](Directory.Packages.props)
- **Environment**: GitHub Actions (Dependabot-managed runner)

## Current Behavior

The most recent scheduled `nuget` run started at `2026-04-27T13:46:25Z`, ran for ~55 minutes inside the `Run Dependabot` step, and was cancelled at `2026-04-27T14:41:39Z` — before producing any PR.

Run: [24998763697](https://github.com/dlrivada/Encina/actions/runs/24998763697).

Likely cause: the repository has ~150+ `.csproj` files across `src/`, `tests/`, `tools/`, and Dependabot must enumerate the dependency graph for each one. With Central Package Management adding cross-project resolution, the analysis exceeds the 1-hour wall clock.

Knock-on effects observed:
- The 3 GHSA advisories patched in #1041 (DataProtection critical, OpenTelemetry moderate ×2) had to be bumped manually.
- Any future advisories landing in dependencies sit unpatched until somebody runs into a red CI.
- The companion `dotnet test` audit only catches them after they break workflows.

## Expected Behavior

Dependabot completes within the timeout and opens PRs automatically when:
1. A package gets a new GHSA advisory, or
2. A grouped update is due per cooldown.

PRs should ship within 24h of an advisory becoming public, not hand-rolled by whoever notices the red CI.

## Impact

- **Developer Experience**: Manual bumps for security advisories instead of reviewing auto-PRs. ~30-60 min per incident, plus the time to debug the failing CI in the first place.
- **CI/CD Time**: N/A — the nuget Dependabot job itself is what's breaking. Other workflows are unaffected directly, but they break later when audit warnings escalate.
- **Reliability**: **Security posture is compromised** — automated security updates are the canonical mitigation path, and that path is currently broken. Critical CVEs (e.g. CVE-2026-40372 in DataProtection) sat unpatched until the regular CI run revealed them.

## Proposed Solution

Investigate and apply one or more of the following, in order of preference:

1. **Group updates aggressively** in [`.github/dependabot.yml`](.github/dependabot.yml) — many updates analyzed together is faster than individual ones. Suggested groups: `microsoft-extensions` (all `Microsoft.Extensions.*`), `efcore` (all `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.*`), `aspnetcore` (all `Microsoft.AspNetCore.*`), `opentelemetry` (`OpenTelemetry.*`), `aws-sdk` (`AWSSDK.*`), `azure-sdk` (`Azure.*`), `testcontainers` (`Testcontainers.*`), `xunit` (`xunit.*`).
2. **Split by directory or ecosystem** — define multiple `package-ecosystem: \"nuget\"` entries scoped to `src/`, `tests/`, `tools/` separately so each runs within budget.
3. **Use cooldown** to reduce churn (`open-pull-requests-limit`, `cooldown.default-days`) and let updates batch up across runs.
4. **Disable transitive analysis** if Dependabot supports a flag — verify against current Dependabot config schema.
5. **Switch to Renovate** if the above fail to bring runs under 60 min — it has more granular timeouts and richer batching, but the migration is non-trivial.

The goal is a **green nuget Dependabot run completing in <60 min**, producing grouped PRs with sensible cadence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Scheduled `nuget` Dependabot run completes within the GitHub timeout
- [ ] At least one auto-generated update PR lands successfully on `main`
- [ ] No regression in update coverage (still picks up all 200+ central packages)
- [ ] Dependabot dashboard / job logs free of timeouts for at least 2 consecutive scheduled runs

## Related Issues / PRs

- #1041 — Manual security bump that motivated this issue (DataProtection 10.0.7, OpenTelemetry 1.15.3). What Dependabot would have raised automatically had it run successfully.
- #1026 — Sibling INFRA issue under v0.13.4 (mutation testing AllTests workaround); shares the "operational quality debt blocking automation" theme.
